name: Tarab / Arrangement Test 01 (BC edge)
description: Batch tarab_test_01: five takes of the same score (moon_101_v2), same seed 101, same cap and lyrics; only the style prompt and lyric stage-directions change. The hypothesis: the B track's 'teamwork' (voice stops, band answers) is described in the training caption ('forward vocals pulling instrumentation down on sustained phrases then band re-enters between lines'), but the moon prompts omitted it. The target is the BC edge: a lead voice that is clearly the star, with a band/second voice that answers in the gaps and never competes. Score each take on its own; do not compare from memory. تقييم الحزمة على محور B–C: صوت رئيسي واضح، وفرقة تجيب في الفراغات ولا تنافس.

criteria.label: Closeness to the BC edge

scale_labels.2: band present but not with the voice
scale_labels.3: halfway — either the star or the answer, not both
scale_labels.4: close — lead in front, band answers
scale_labels.5: B/C level — memorable and clearly a lead voice with a responsive band

criteria.help: The target, in one sentence: a lead singer who is unmistakably the star, plus a band or second voice that answers only in the gaps. Not A's default. This is the metric the batch is ranked by.

criteria.label: Overall quality

scale_labels.5: Excellent — would play it for someone

criteria.help: Your gut call on the whole take, independent of the hypothesis.

criteria.label: Is the lead singer the star?

scale_labels.5: Alone in front, loud and clear

criteria.help: Ignore whether you like the tune. Just: who owns the track? C is 5. A is around 2–3.

criteria.label: When the singer pauses, does the band answer before he returns?

scale_labels.1: Never — the gap stays empty or the band noodles
scale_labels.5: Every line — a short, clear answer in the gap

criteria.help: This is the B behaviour at 0:43.7–0:46.1: the voice stops, the guitar answers for 1–2 seconds, then gets out of the way. Count the answers, not the length of the solos.

criteria.label: Is the arrangement sparse enough for the voice?

scale_labels.1: Crowded — everyone playing all the time

criteria.help: C was praised as 'not a busy song'. A busy mix can still be loud; this asks whether there is room around the voice.

criteria.label: Is there a second voice?

options.t: Clear backing that answers the lead

criteria.help: B's description: backing vocals come and go, felt more than seen, trading half-lines with the lead. C has none. Tick what you actually hear.

criteria.label: Does the vocal feel tarab / Arabic in character?

scale_labels.5: Unmistakably tarab, no traditional instruments needed

criteria.help: The feeling, not theory. Do not name a maqam or count accidentals. B is the reference; C's chorus is the other reference.

criteria.label: Different from the usual out-of-the-box take?

scale_labels.5: Its own thing — would not guess it came from the same batch

criteria.help: Your 5-star sentence was 'the music feels different'. This asks how different, relative to the A family.

criteria.label: Is there a moment you would replay or hum?

scale_labels.5: A specific line or fill I would replay

criteria.help: Name the timestamp in Notes if you can. For B this was the line at 1:51.6 and the fill at 0:43.7.

criteria.label: Diction / pronunciation
criteria.help: Whole-line collapse is an automatic low score here, regardless of how good the music is.

criteria.label: Mix quality
criteria.help: Balance, clarity, reverb, stereo width. Judge the sound, not the composition.

criteria.label: Notes
criteria.help: Timestamps, which line stuck, where the band answered, wrong words, anything. Plain words.
